coding_context.description: The replication tested the impact of need for cognition on message evaluation, showing that individuals high in need for cognition evaluate strong arguments more favorably and are less influenced by weak arguments compared to those low in need for cognition.
coding_context.reported_success_quote:
Across the in-lab replication studies (N =

2,365),9 participants found stronger arguments to be more compelling
than weaker arguments, F(1, 2361) = 79.925, p b .001, ηp
2 = 0.033,

95% CI = [.020, .048].10 However, unlike the original study, the interac-
tion term was not reliably different from zero, F(1, 2361) = 0.129, p =

.720, ηp
2 = 5.46 e-5, 95% CI = [0, .002].11
